label: Aquinas, I q.7 a.2 co.: Condition on a created form subsisting apart from matter
interpretation: Aquinas considers the conditional case of a created form subsisting apart from matter. Such a form would be infinite in the respect of lacking a material bound, yet finite absolutely because it has esse received and contracted to a determinate nature.
attribution: The passage states that if a created form subsists apart from matter, its esse is received and contracted to a determinate nature, which is the premise.
